title: Squad Atlas Onboarding
description: Your week-one essentials for joining Squad Atlas (Payments) at Meridian — on-call, compliance, releases, data, architecture, and ownership.

questions.prompt: Which tool does Squad Atlas use to run its on-call paging rotation?
questions.explanation: Atlas runs its on-call rotation through Opsgenie (Squad Atlas — On-Call Runbook). PagerDuty is Borealis, Splunk On-Call is Cypress, and the org-wide VictorOps policy was retired in 2024.

questions.prompt: What is the acknowledgement SLA on an Atlas page before it escalates to the secondary?
questions.explanation: Atlas pages have a 10-minute ack SLA; miss it and Opsgenie escalates to the secondary, then the squad lead (Squad Atlas — On-Call Runbook). Cypress holds 5 minutes and Borealis 15.

questions.prompt: An alert fires for a failed payment settlement on Atlas. What severity is it?
questions.explanation: Any settlement failure is money movement impacted, so it is always Sev1 — never downgrade to Sev2 because 'only a few payments' failed (Squad Atlas — On-Call Runbook).

questions.prompt: Which compliance regime does Squad Atlas operate under?
questions.explanation: Because Atlas handles cardholder data directly, it operates under PCI-DSS Level 1, the strictest tier (Squad Atlas — Compliance & Data Handling). Org-wide 'SOC 2 only' is a superseded 2023 baseline; SOX is Borealis and KYC/AML is Cypress.

questions.prompt: How is card data classified under Atlas's data-classification scheme?
questions.explanation: Card data is Tier 0 (Restricted), Meridian's highest tier — never logged, never in error messages, never leaving PCI scope (Squad Atlas — Compliance & Data Handling). Tier 1 is the lending/identity squads; 'Sensitive' is the retired two-tier scheme.

questions.prompt: What is Atlas's production deploy-window policy?
choices: Deploy any weekday; no fixed windows
No deploys on Friday or over the weekend
questions.explanation: The Atlas pipeline is gated to refuse production releases Friday through Sunday because settlement runs continuously (Squad Atlas — Release & Change Policy). The 9–5 freeze is Cypress; 'deploy any weekday' is Borealis; 'self-merge anytime' is a superseded pre-2024 policy.

questions.prompt: How many approvals does a production change to Atlas require before release?
choices: No approval — self-merge once CI is green
questions.explanation: Atlas requires dual approval — two engineers, one of whom has context on the area being changed (Squad Atlas — Release & Change Policy). Single approval is Borealis; self-merge is the retired pre-2024 model.

questions.prompt: Which mandatory pre-merge check must pass before an Atlas pull request can merge?
questions.explanation: The ledger-reconciliation contract test verifies recorded entries match settled balances; a red result blocks merge with no override (Squad Atlas — Release & Change Policy). The credit-model backtest is Borealis and the sanctions-screening test is Cypress.

questions.prompt: What is the primary datastore behind atlas-ledger-svc?
questions.explanation: Atlas's primary datastore is Aurora PostgreSQL, giving strong consistency and durability for money movement (Squad Atlas — Architecture & Datastores). DynamoDB is Borealis, Neo4j is Cypress, and shared MySQL was the decommissioned legacy monolith.

questions.prompt: How does atlas-ledger-svc record a correction to the ledger?
choices: It updates the existing ledger row in place
It deletes the row and re-inserts a corrected one
It appends a new entry that offsets the prior one
It edits the shared reporting table directly
questions.explanation: The ledger is append-only: rows are never updated or deleted in place — corrections are new entries that offset prior ones, keeping a full reconstructable history (Squad Atlas — Architecture & Datastores).

questions.prompt: What is the name of Squad Atlas's primary service — the codebase you'll spend most of your time in?
questions.explanation: atlas-ledger-svc owns the ledger, settlement workers, and reconciliation logic (Squad Atlas — Charter & Ownership). payments-monolith was decommissioned in 2024; the others belong to Borealis and Cypress.

questions.prompt: What is the internal codename for Atlas's payment-initiation API?
questions.explanation: Rail is the internal name for the payment-initiation endpoint on atlas-ledger-svc — all payment initiation flows through it (Squad Atlas — Charter & Ownership). Bridge is Borealis, Gateway is Cypress, and PayGT was the legacy monolith's API.

questions.prompt: Who is the squad lead and engineering manager of Squad Atlas?
questions.explanation: Priya Nair leads Atlas and is the escalation point for ownership disputes and payment-path commitments; book a week-one 1:1 with her (Squad Atlas — Charter & Ownership). Dana Whitfield leads Cypress and Marco Reyes leads Borealis.

questions.prompt: Where does Squad Atlas store its secrets?
choices: A .env file checked into the repo
Vault, under a per-squad atlas/ namespace
questions.explanation: All Atlas secrets live in Vault under the dedicated per-squad namespace atlas/; services read them at runtime and nothing is stored outside it (Squad Atlas — Secrets & Access). Borealis uses AWS Secrets Manager and cypress/ belongs to Cypress.

questions.prompt: What customer-facing SLA does Atlas publish for payment status availability?
questions.explanation: Atlas publishes a 99.95% monthly SLA — customers must be able to see a payment's state (pending, settled, failed) within that target every calendar month; a breach triggers a customer-facing comms review (Squad Atlas — Charter & Ownership).
